## What This Is

The China Semiconductor Tracker is a curated, open-source resource monitoring semiconductor manufacturing facilities, chip design firms, and equipment/materials suppliers across mainland China.

It is maintained by [Pranay Kotasthane](https://pranaykotas.com) at the [Takshashila Institution](https://takshashila.org.in), part of Takshashila's **[Siliconpolitik Project](https://takshashila.org.in/pages/research-areas/focus-areas/siliconpolitik.html)**. It is a companion to the [India Semiconductor Tracker](https://fabs.pranaykotas.com).

## Scope

This tracker covers mainland China (PRC) only. Taiwan and the Taiwanese semiconductor ecosystem are out of scope — a distinct political and market story that would need its own tracker.

## Naming Convention

Facility, company, design-firm, and equipment/materials-firm names are given in three forms where verified: English, simplified Chinese (简体), and Hanyu Pinyin. City and province names are given in English only. An entry showing "Chinese name not yet verified" reflects a genuine data gap, not an editorial choice.

## Units

Investment figures are shown in **¥ (RMB) 亿 (100 million yuan)** — the unit Chinese financial press and company filings typically report in — with a dollar figure alongside where a firm's investment is only disclosed in USD.

## Sourcing Strategy

- **Listed-company filings** (SMIC and Hua Hong on HKEX/SSE) are treated as primary sources for financials and capacity, sourced via exchange disclosures or cninfo.com.cn.
- **Chinese financial and industry press** (Caixin, 21世纪经济报道) is cited directly, with the same scrutiny applied to any credible outlet.
- **State media** (Xinhua, CCTV, People's Daily) is treated as a primary source for the fact of an announcement, not for its interpretation — the same standard applied to a government press release from any country.
- **Export-control evasion, smuggled equipment, and actual sanctioned-node yields** are structurally under-covered by domestic sources; these rely on SemiAnalysis, BIS Federal Register entries, and investigative reporting (Reuters, Nikkei Asia, FT).
- **LLM tools (including DeepSeek) are used only as research aids** — locating candidate sources, translating filings, summarizing documents — never cited as the source of a fact. Every figure traces to a cited source; where a source only gave year- or month-level precision, this site displays that same precision rather than a fabricated exact day.
- **Conflicting reports are stated, not silently resolved.** Where independent sources disagree on a figure or a facility's current status (for example, JHICC's production status, or SMIC Beijing's investment figure varying by roughly $0.1B across outlets), the disagreement is noted directly in that entry's narrative rather than picking one number without comment.

## Technical Complexity Index

Each facility is scored 1 (low) to 5 (high), benchmarked against a cutting-edge 3nm fab (5/5): composite = Technology Difficulty (55%) + Capital Intensity (45%).

## Export-Control Designations

Two distinct US designations appear on this site where relevant: the Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) **Entity List**, which restricts exports of controlled items, and the Department of Defense's **Section 1260H list** of Chinese military-linked companies, a disclosure designation with different legal consequences. Each flagged entry names which list applies — see [Policy & Budget](budget.qmd).

## Data Status

As of `r format(Sys.Date(), "%B %Y")`, this tracker covers `r nrow(load_facilities("data/facilities.yml"))` facilities, `r nrow(load_design_firms("data/design.yml"))` chip design firms, and `r nrow(load_materials_firms("data/materials.yml"))` equipment/materials firms — Phase 1's initial batches, built to exercise every page and field in the schema end to end rather than to reach full national coverage.

Known gaps queued for a future research batch, not omitted by oversight: the remaining facilities toward China's full national count of 100+ fabs, plus specific named candidates not yet researched to this tracker's sourcing standard — Wingtech/Nexperia's China operations, GTA Semiconductor, and TCL Zhonghuan (a separate silicon wafer maker from National Silicon Industry Group, already covered). **Highest priority for the next batch:** SMIC's own primary advanced-node Shanghai fab (its Pudong SN1/SN2 lines, the facility actually behind the Kirin 9000S / 7nm export-control story) — this tracker's current `smic-lingang` entry covers a separate, newer, less-advanced 28nm joint venture in Shanghai's Lingang area, not that flagship fab. See the project's GitHub repository for current status.

**Foreign-invested facilities:** this tracker now covers the major foreign-owned fabs physically located in mainland China — Samsung Xi'an (NAND), SK Hynix Wuxi (DRAM) and Dalian (NAND, a former Intel fab), Intel Chengdu (assembly/test only, no fab), TSMC Nanjing and Shanghai, and UMC Xiamen. Checked and explicitly ruled out: GlobalFoundries cancelled its planned Chengdu fab in 2018 before it ever became operational and has no current fab in mainland China. Not yet added: foreign equipment makers' service, repair, and R&D centers in China (Applied Materials' Xi'an and Shanghai sites, ASML's Beijing repair center, Lam Research's Shanghai training center) — these support existing tools rather than manufacture new ones, a meaningfully different kind of facility from the equipment-maker entries already in this tracker, and were judged lower priority for this batch than the fabs above.
